canonical_name: Odd order theorem for finite groups
literal_source_claim_en: Groups of odd order are solvable.
source_attribution: Walter Feit and John G. Thompson, 1963
canonical_statement: Every finite group of odd order is solvable.
canonical_claim: Every finite group of odd order is solvable.

canonical_formal_target.candidate_expression: {G : Type u} -> [Group G] -> [Finite G] -> Odd (Nat.card G) -> IsSolvable G

domain_and_universes: G : Type u in an arbitrary universe, with ordered Group G and Finite G typeclass binders, followed by an explicit Odd (Nat.card G) premise; no nontriviality, simplicity, or commutativity assumption.
quantifiers: for every finite multiplicative group G
hypotheses: the carrier of G is finite
the natural-number cardinality of G is odd
conclusion: G is solvable, represented by mathlib's IsSolvable predicate and checked equivalent to eventual triviality of derivedSeries.
degenerate_case_status: No finite odd-order group is excluded. Generic boundary implications check inclusion of groups of order one and all finite commutative odd-order groups; the order-one exclusion mutation is rejected.
candidate_scope_not_credited: the checked Fintype.card, modulo-two, and derived-series forms are alternate encodings, not additional proof targets
the externally machine-checked Coq/MathComp theorem before immutable dependency and cross-system integration review
excluded_substitutions: solvability only for commutative groups, Z-groups, groups of prime order, or another special class
Burnside's p^a q^b theorem or a fixed finite-order case
classification of finite simple groups or only the simple odd-order corollary
odd order of an element, automorphism, character, graph, or other object rather than the group carrier
a premise or data structure that assumes IsSolvable G
the Coq/MathComp result reported as Lean kernel closure without pin/import/check integration
